title: Re: Coordinating demo time for Acme Robotics (Tokyo/Sydney timezone mismatch)
text:
Re: Coordinating demo time for Acme Robotics (Tokyo/Sydney timezone mismatch)

['From: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:32:00 +0900
Subject: Demo availability — APAC hours (Tokyo / Sydney)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for getting back to us. Were excited to see Redwood in action — a few people on our side will join from Tokyo (JST) and Sydney (AEDT). To avoid late nights, our availability window (local times) next week is:

- Tokyo: 09:30–12:00 JST
- Sydney: 10:30–13:00 AEDT

I attached a quick availability grid (CSV) and an .ics with the two preferred slots we tried to add to a tentative calendar. Can you propose a slot that works for your team? Preferably Mon or Tue next week (Dec 7–8).

Also, a quick note: our admin sometimes sees invites appear on the previous day for Sydney folks when invites come from US timezones — happy to be explicit about local times in the subject.

Thanks,
Kenji Sato
Head of Integration — Acme Robotics
kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp
+81 90 1234 5678

Attachments:
- acme_availability_grid.csv (CSV)
- prospect_availability.ics (calendar file)', 'From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo availability — APAC hours (Tokyo / Sydney)

Hi Kenji — thanks for the availability.

Quick note: your .ics imported fine into my calendar, but my GCal defaulted to PST (my laptop is set to San Francisco), which showed the slot as the previous evening here. Im proposing two confirmed slots (I converted to local times to avoid confusion):

Option A: Tue Dec 8, 10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT — 45 minutes
Option B: Tue Dec 8, 11:30 JST / 12:30 AEDT — 45 minutes

If either works please confirm and Ill send a calendar invite with local times in the subject and a note about timezones. Ill include a brief demo deck and who will join from our side.

Also looping Karthik and Soojin to confirm the run-of-show and to make sure were not overlooking any regional compliance questions.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-demo-deck.pdf (preview)

> On Nov 29, 2026, at 09:32, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp> wrote:
> > (original message and attachments)', 'From: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Demo availability — APAC hours (Tokyo / Sydney)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks — Option A looks perfect for the Tokyo folks, but Maya in Sydney is seeing the invite as Mon Dec 7 13:00 AEDT in her calendar (shes on Google Calendar). She forwarded me the invite and it shows PST as the creators timezone. I think when your calendar created the event it defaulted to your local timezone and Google translated it, which ended up as the previous day in Sydney for some participants.

Can you please:
- Recreate the invite explicitly set to Dec 8, 10:00 JST / Dec 8, 11:00 AEDT (explicit timezone fields)
- Put the local times in the subject line like: "Dec 8 (10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT) — Redwood demo for Acme"

Maya also asked whether the recording will be available afterwards as she may need to forward to a colleague in Melbourne whos on a different shift.

Kenji

> On Nov 29, 2026, at 18:06, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > (proposed slots)', 'From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:44:00 +0530
Subject: Fwd: Acme demo — timezone/subject convention suggestion

Vivek — quick internal note before you recreate the invite:

1) Use explicit TZ IDs when creating the Google Calendar event (Asia/Tokyo and Australia/Sydney). Dont rely on auto-conversion.
2) Add the phrase "(local times listed)" at the top of the invite description and in the subject like Kenji suggested.
3) Mark the invite as being sent from the Redwood APAC alias (apac-demos@redwood.ai) if possible — that often prevents display oddities when recipients have mixed orgs.

I can send the invite from the APAC alias if you want — Im in IST so I can make the booking within your requested window without hitting midnight for me.

Also, we usually include a short note on recordings: we record demos and post to a secure link for 30 days for prospects. That should be fine to tell Maya.

Karthik

Attachments: none', 'From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 09:05:00 +1100
Subject: Confirmed: Dec 8 (10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT) — Redwood demo for Acme Robotics

Hi Kenji / Maya — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Confirmed: Tue Dec 8, 10:00–10:45 JST / 11:00–11:45 AEDT.

Notes:
- Invite sent from apac-demos@redwood.ai (should display Asia/Tokyo + Australia/Sydney correctly).
- Subject: "Dec 8 (10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT) — Redwood demo for Acme Robotics"
- Recording: we will record and post a secure link (available for 30 days).
- Joining from Redwood: Vivek (AE), Karthik (Solutions), Soojin (Platform PM), Tessa (CS).

I attached the finalized calendar .ics for manual import if needed and the demo deck. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Vivek

Attachments:
- prospect_availability.ics (finalized invite)
- redwood-demo-deck.pdf (final)

> On Nov 30, 2026, at 10:12, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp> wrote:
> > (asked to recreate invite)', 'From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@acmerobotics.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acmerobotics.jp>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 22:05:00 +1100
Subject: Re: Confirmed: Dec 8 (10:00 JST / 11:00 AEDT) — Redwood demo for Acme Robotics

Thanks Vivek — I can confirm on my side. Recording note is perfect.

Small request: can you also include the meeting times in ISO date/time in the invite body (e.g., 2026-12-08T10:00:00+09:00 and 2026-12-08T11:00:00+11:00)? A couple of our engineers import invites into internal tooling that expects ISO timestamps.

Appreciate the clarity — see you then.

Maya

--
Maya Chen
Technical Program Manager, Acme Robotics
maya.chen@acmerobotics.com
', '']
